findings.title: Slots inside a date-override window bypass the busy-time check, allowing double bookings on override days
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches one of the host's date overrides and the slot falls inside the override window, the function executes `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom of the function. Since timeSlots produced by getSlots are generated purely from working hours/overrides and the ONLY place busy times (calendar events and existing Cal bookings) are applied is this function, a host with a date override on a given day will show every slot inside the override window as available even if they already have bookings or calendar events at those times. This applies to both fixed hosts and round-robin hosts (both call sites spread `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`, which includes dateOverrides), so this reintroduces double-booking on exactly the days users most often override (vacation/partial-day blocks). The override branch should verify the working-hours/override window and then still fall through to the busy check instead of returning true unconditionally.

findings.title: Dayjs instances compared with === never match; start==end override branch is dead code
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly constructed Dayjs object instances with strict equality, which is always false regardless of the underlying times. The intent is clearly to detect overrides where start equals end (the 'blocked' override case) and mark all slots unavailable, but this branch can never execute. As a result, such overrides are handled only by the general before/after conditions, and a slot that straddles the override's start instant (slotStart < start < slotEnd) slips through as available. The comparison must use `.isSame()` or compare `.valueOf()`/`.diff()`.

findings.title: Working-hours check uses slot start time for both start and end, ignoring event length
findings.body: In the new working-hours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` compute the identical value — `end` is a copy-paste of `start` and never adds the event length. The check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` therefore only validates that the slot's *start* minute is inside the fixed host's working hours. For a round-robin event, timeSlots are generated from the union of all hosts' availability, so a slot can start inside a fixed host's window but run past that host's working-hours end (e.g., host A works until 12:30 UTC, host B until 13:00; a 60-minute slot at 12:00 generated from B's frame passes A's check). This is exactly the class of bug the PR claims to fix — fixed hosts being bookable when unavailable — and it still leaks through at the end-of-day boundary. `end` should be computed from `slotEndTime` (start + eventLength).

findings.title: Days with no working-hours entry are treated as fully available for fixed hosts
findings.body: The working-hours check only excludes a slot when `workingHours.find(...)` locates a working-hour entry whose `days` array includes the slot's weekday and whose time range excludes the slot. If the fixed host has no working-hours entry at all for the slot's day (e.g., the host works Mon–Fri while a round-robin co-host also works weekends), `find` returns undefined, the exclusion branch is skipped, and the slot proceeds to the busy check — i.e., the host is considered available on their day off. Since round-robin slot generation uses the union of all hosts' availability, weekend slots generated from other hosts will be offered with a fixed host who never works that day. The logic should treat 'no working hour covering this slot's day/time' as unavailable, not just 'a same-day working hour exists but the time is outside it'.

findings.title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC timezones
findings.body: The day-match test compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is explicitly UTC (`time.utc()`), but `dayjs(date.start)` parses the Date in the server's local timezone and `format()` renders in that same local zone. On any server not running in UTC, the two day strings can disagree for overrides/slots near midnight, causing overrides to be attached to the wrong calendar day (slots on the override day treated as normal working hours and vice versa). The override instant should be normalized with `dayjs.utc(date.start)` before the day comparison.

findings.title: No automated test for the headline fix: round-robin event with a fixed host's date override
findings.body: The PR's primary purpose (issue #8207) is making date overrides of fixed hosts restrict round-robin availability, but the only test added covers the timezone conversion of an override on a single-user personal event. There is no test creating a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host plus a loose host and a date override on the fixed host, so regressions of the core fix would not be caught. Additionally, there is no test combining a date override with an existing booking or calendar busy time on the same day — such a test would have exposed that checkIfIsAvailable returns early (before the busy check) for slots inside an override window, permitting double bookings.
